_note: MOCK DATA. These codes are modeled on real, publicly documented EPFO rejection categories (news reports, EPFO circulars, claimant forums) but the exact code strings are fictionalized for this prototype. No real EPFO API, portal, or claimant data was accessed.

codes.rawPortalText: Claim Rejected. Reason: KYC Not Approved.
codes.plainLanguage: Your Aadhaar, PAN or bank details are linked to your account, but your employer hasn't digitally verified them yet. Until they do, EPFO won't release funds — even though your documents are correct.
codes.actorLabel: Your employer's EPFO admin needs to act
fixSteps: Log in and check the KYC tab — if Aadhaar/PAN/Bank all show a green tick, your documents are fine.
The pending step is your employer's DSC (Digital Signature Certificate) approval on their EPFO employer portal.
Message your HR/payroll contact with your UAN and ask them to approve pending KYC under 'Member KYC Approval'.
Once approved, no need to refile — the same claim auto-resumes processing.
codes.typicalTurnaround: 3–7 working days after employer approves, if no other issues

codes.rawPortalText: Claim Rejected. Reason: Details do not match Aadhaar records.
codes.plainLanguage: The name on your EPFO/UAN profile doesn't exactly match the name on your Aadhaar — even a missing middle name, extra initial, or different spelling triggers this.
fixSteps: Compare your UAN profile name letter-by-letter against your Aadhaar card.
If they differ, raise a 'Joint Declaration' request with your employer via the portal to correct your EPFO name to match Aadhaar exactly.
Alternatively, update your Aadhaar name to match your EPFO records via UIDAI if the EPFO version is the correct one.
Resubmit the claim only after the corrected name shows on both records — resubmitting before that repeats the rejection.
codes.typicalTurnaround: 5–10 working days for the name correction to reflect, then normal claim processing

codes.rawPortalText: Claim Rejected. Reason: Bank details verification failed.
codes.plainLanguage: The bank account number or IFSC code linked to your UAN doesn't match a real, active account — often because a branch merged and its IFSC changed, or a digit was mistyped years ago.
fixSteps: Download a current bank statement or passbook copy less than 3 months old.
Go to 'Manage > KYC' and update your bank account number and IFSC exactly as printed on the statement.
If your branch merged recently, look up the new IFSC on your bank's website — old codes silently fail verification.
Wait for the new bank KYC to show 'Approved', then resubmit the claim.
codes.typicalTurnaround: 2–4 working days for bank re-verification, then normal claim processing

codes.rawPortalText: Claim Rejected. Reason: Date of exit not marked by employer.
codes.plainLanguage: EPFO doesn't know you've actually left your last job — your employer never marked your exit date, so the system assumes you're still employed and blocks withdrawal.
codes.actorLabel: Your former employer needs to act
fixSteps: Check your Service History tab — if your last employment shows no 'Date of Exit', this is the cause.
If it's been over 2 months since you left, you can self-declare your exit date on the portal.
If it's under 2 months, you'll need your former employer to mark it — send them a written request citing your relieving date.
Resubmit once the exit date appears against your last employer entry.
codes.typicalTurnaround: Immediate if self-declared after 2 months; 7–14 days if waiting on employer

codes.rawPortalText: Claim Rejected. Reason: Form 15G/15H not submitted.
codes.plainLanguage: You're withdrawing before 5 years of continuous service and your balance is above the tax-free threshold, so EPFO needs a signed declaration to avoid deducting TDS at the higher rate — you just weren't told this before you filed.
fixSteps: Download Form 15G (or 15H if you're a senior citizen) — it's a self-declaration that your total income is below the taxable limit.
Fill in your PAN, estimated total income for the year, and sign.
Upload it in the claim's document section, or attach it while refiling.
If your income is actually above the taxable limit, skip this — TDS will simply apply and the claim proceeds without the form.
codes.typicalTurnaround: 1–3 working days after the form is attached

codes.shortLabel: Multiple UANs Linked to Same Aadhaar
codes.rawPortalText: Claim Rejected. Reason: Multiple active UANs detected.
codes.plainLanguage: You have more than one UAN — usually from an employer issuing a fresh one instead of reusing your existing account when you switched jobs. EPFO freezes withdrawal until the accounts are merged.
fixSteps: Go to 'One Employee One EPF Account' on the portal and check for other UANs linked to your Aadhaar or PAN.
Submit a merger request — you'll need basic KYC for both UANs on hand.
This typically triggers a manual review by a regional EPFO officer.
Once merged, your full service history and balance combine, and the claim can be refiled against the single active UAN.
codes.typicalTurnaround: 15–30 working days — this one genuinely takes longest, and the portal doesn't say so upfront
